Timmy demanded, "Please birdie, I'm so lonely. Can't you stay and play with me?"

The birdie thought for a moment and said, "Okay, I'll stay and play with you for a little while. But then I have to go back to my family."

Timmy was so happy to have a friend to play with. They played together for a while, but then the birdie had to go back to its family. Timmy said goodbye and thanked the birdie for being his friend. From that day on, Timmy wasn't as lonely because he knew he had a friend in the little birdie.

A few days later, Lily had a test at school. She studied really hard and used her dictionary to learn new words. When she got her test back, she saw that she got a perfect score! She was so successful! She ran home and told her mommy, "Mommy, I pushed myself to study and I was successful!" Her mommy was so proud of her.

Lily's mommy tried to comfort her and waved her hand to say goodbye to the doctor. But Lily was still upset and didn't want to leave. As they walked out of the doctor's office, Lily tripped and fell. She hurt her knee and started to cry even more.

Once upon a time, there was a little firefly named Sparky. Sparky had a battery inside him that made him glow bright like a star. One day, Sparky went out to play with his firefly friends. They flew around the field and played hide-and-seek. 

Suddenly, a fierce wind blew and Sparky got separated from his friends. He was scared and didn't know where to go. But then, he remembered his battery and how it made him glow. So, he turned it on and shone brightly. His friends saw his glow from far away and came to find him. 

From that day on, Sparky always made sure his battery was charged so he could glow and never get lost again. He and his friends continued to play and have fun in the field, glowing brightly in the night sky.

A man was walking his dog near the park. He saw Lily and Tom fighting over the stick. He came over and said, "Hey, kids, what are you doing? Why are you fighting over a stick? That is not nice. That is bad. You should be kind and gentle to each other. You should share and take turns. Can you explain why you want the stick so much?"

Lily and Tom stopped pulling the stick. They looked at the man and his dog. They felt a little ashamed. They did not have a good reason to fight over the stick. They just wanted it. They said, "Sorry, mister. We were being bad. We wanted the stick because it is fun and big and we can use it for many things. But we did not think about the other person. We did not ask or listen. We were selfish and rude."

The man smiled and said, "That is okay, kids. I am glad you are sorry. You are not bad. You are good. You just made a mistake. We all make mistakes sometimes. But we can learn from them and do better next time. How about you give the stick to my dog? He likes to play with sticks too. He can fetch and chew and wag his tail. He will be very happy. And you can play with each other or with other toys. There are many things to do in the park. You can have fun and be friends. What do you say?"

Lily and Tom smiled and said, "Thank you, mister. Thank you, dog. You are very nice. We are sorry for fighting. We will share and take turns. We will be kind and gentle. We will have fun and be friends."

The man and his dog waved and walked away. Lily and Tom hugged and said, "We are sorry, too. We are friends. We love each other. We love the park. We love to play." They ran and jumped and slid and laughed. They had a good time. They learned a lesson. They were happy. The end.

Lily and Ben were twins who lived on a farm. They liked to play with the animals, but sometimes they were naughty. One day, they saw a new cow in the barn. The cow was big and brown and had a bell around her neck.

"Let's go and say hello to the new cow!" Lily said.

"OK, but be careful. She might not like us," Ben said.

They ran to the barn and climbed over the fence. The cow was eating some hay and did not see them. Lily and Ben crept closer and closer. They wanted to touch the cow's bell and make it ring.

"Boo!" Lily shouted and pulled the bell. The cow was scared and mooed loudly. She kicked her legs and ran away. Lily and Ben laughed and chased after her.

"Stop! Stop!" they heard a voice. It was their dad. He was angry and worried. He caught Lily and Ben and took them back to the fence.

"What are you doing? You scared the new cow! She is not used to our farm. You have to be gentle and kind to her. She is our guest. You have to welcome her, not frighten her," he said.

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They did not mean to be bad. They wanted to have fun.

"We are sorry, dad. We did not know. We wanted to play with the new cow," they said.

Dad sighed and hugged them.

"I know, but you have to think of how the animals feel. They have feelings too. They need love and respect. The new cow is very shy and nervous. She needs time to get used to us. Maybe you can help me feed her and brush her. Then she will trust us and be happy here," he said.

Lily and Ben nodded. They wanted to be good and help dad. They wanted to make friends with the new cow.

"Can we say sorry to the new cow, dad?" they asked.

"Of course. Come on, let's go and find her. Maybe she will let you pet her and give her a name," dad said.

They followed dad to the field where the new cow was grazing. She looked up and saw them. She was still a bit scared, but she did not run away. Lily and Ben smiled and waved.

"Hello, new cow. We are sorry we scared you. We want to welcome you to our farm. We want to be your friends. What is your name?" they said.

The cow mooed softly and came closer. She sniffed Lily and Ben and licked their hands. They giggled and stroked her fur. She felt warm and soft.

"I think she likes us, dad," Lily said.

"I think so too. And I think I have a name for her. How about Bella? It means beautiful and it sounds like her bell," dad said.

Lily and Ben liked the name. They repeated it and the cow mooed again.

"Bella, Bella, Bella. You are a beautiful cow. We are happy you are here. We will be nice to you and take care of you," they said.

Bella nodded and nuzzled them. She felt happy and safe. She had a new home and new friends.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the children to be respectful and kind to animals, especially new ones. It also shows them how to apologize and make amends for their mistakes. It also encourages them to welcome and befriend others who are different from them.

Lily felt a little bad, but she also felt a little proud. She had made something big vanish. That was a success. She smiled and said, "No, I won't. It's my wand. I can do what I want."

Ben felt angry and sad. He liked his car. He wanted it back. He also felt envious. He wished he had the wand. He said, "That's mean, Lily. You're not my friend anymore. Give me the wand!"

They started to tug and pull on the wand. They both wanted it. They shouted and cried. They did not notice the wand was glowing.

Suddenly, there was a flash of light. Lily and Ben vanished. The wand fell to the ground. It was quiet and still.

Mia tries. "Te quiero. Te quiero, Sam. Te quiero, grandma."

Sam claps. "Very good, Mia. You are smart. Grandma will be happy to hear you. Do you want to send her a letter too?"

Mia nods again. She wants to send grandma a letter. She wants to say 'te quiero' and 'thank you' and 'hello'. She also wants to draw a picture of her and Sam and grandma.

Sam helps Mia. They write and draw a letter for grandma. They put it in an envelope. They write grandma's name and address. They put a stamp on it. They go to the mailbox. They put the letter inside.

"Bye bye, letter. Have a good trip. Say hello to grandma." Mia says.

Sam hugs Mia. "You are a good friend, Mia. Grandma will love your letter. She will send you a letter back. Maybe she will send you a sticker and a candy too."

Mia smiles. She is happy. She likes Sam and grandma. She likes Spanish. She likes letters. She hopes grandma gets her letter soon.

She was so excited to be there and explore what it was like to live in such a beautiful place.

Once there was a friendly fox called Toby. He liked to play in the garden, and he had many friends who liked to play with him too. One day when he was playing, Toby found a rocket. He was surprised and excited, and he decided to take the rocket home with him.

On his way home, Toby forgot all about the rocket. As he walked, he decided to have a snack. Toby was so busy eating, he forgot to keep track of the time.

Just then, Toby's friend Lenny came out and saw him. "Hey Toby!" shouted Lenny, "don't forget about the rocket!"

Toby remembered the rocket and he apologised to Lenny for forgetting about it. From then on, Toby made sure he kept track of his time, and remembered to take his things with him.

The moral of the story is: always remember to take care of your things, even when you are having fun.

Once upon a time there was a small girl. Everyday she would play in a big, green field near the stream. She loved spending time listening to the stream, watching the fish swim, and feeling the sun on her face.

One day she decided to explore. She walked along the bank of the stream until she came to a big yummy fruit tree. She climbed the tree and, without looking, grabbed a handful of fruit from the branches.

The girl knew she should not have done that because the fruits were not hers. She felt scared. Without thinking, she quickly reversed back the way she had come with the fruit still in her hands.

Suddenly, she heard a loud rumbling sound. When she looked fearfully around, she noticed that the stream was now flowing in the opposite direction. Its power was so great that the little girl could not escape. She was sadly swept away in the fast flowing stream, never to be seen again. 

The moral of this story is to think before you act. No matter how much you want something, if it isn't yours you should not take it. Instincts won't always lead to safety either, so it is always wise to think ahead.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they found some dry leaves and sticks in the yard. They wanted to make a fire, like they saw on TV. They piled up the leaves and sticks and looked for a match.

"Here, I have one," Sam said. He took a match from his pocket and struck it on a rock. The match lit up and he threw it on the pile. The leaves and sticks caught fire and made a big flame.

"Wow, look at that!" Tim said. He was excited and scared at the same time. The fire was hot and bright and made a crackling sound.

But the fire was also dangerous. The wind blew and the fire spread to the grass and the flowers. The fire was getting bigger and bigger and closer and closer to the house.

"Help, help!" Tim and Sam shouted. They were afraid and sorry. They ran away from the fire and looked for their mom.

Mom heard their cries and came out of the house. She saw the fire and was very angry and worried. She grabbed a hose and sprayed water on the fire. She put out the fire and saved the house.

"Tim, Sam, what have you done?" Mom asked. She was stern and sad. "You could have burned the house and hurt yourselves. You know you are not allowed to play with fire. Fire is terrible and dangerous. You are very naughty boys."

Tim and Sam felt ashamed and guilty. They knew they had made a big mistake. They hugged their mom and said they were sorry.

"We are sorry, Mom," they said. "We were curious and foolish. We will never play with fire again. Please forgive us."

Mom was still angry, but she also loved her sons. She hugged them back and said she forgave them.

"I forgive you, but you have to promise me you will never play with fire again," she said. "And you have to help me clean up the mess you made. You have to scatter the ashes and plant new flowers. Do you understand?"

Tim and Sam nodded and said they understood. They learned their lesson and never played with fire again. They helped their mom scatter the ashes and plant new flowers. They were sorry for the fire, but happy for their mom.

Sam likes to play with his toy cop car. He makes the siren sound and drives it around the room. He pretends he is a strong cop who helps people and catches bad guys.

One day, he sees a real cop car outside his window. He runs to the window and watches the cop car. He sees a cop get out of the car and talk to a man. The man looks angry and scared. The cop says something to the man, but Sam cannot hear what he says.

Sam wants to know what the cop says. He grabs his toy cop car and runs to the door. He opens the door and runs outside. He follows the cop and the man. He tries to get closer to hear them.

The cop sees Sam and stops talking. He looks at Sam and smiles. He says, "Hello, little boy. What are you doing here?"

Sam holds up his toy cop car and says, "I am a cop too. I want to hear what you say to the man."

The cop laughs and says, "Well, I am asking the man some questions. He was driving too fast and he broke a rule. He has to pay a fine and be more careful next time."

Sam nods and says, "I see. Can I repeat what you say to the man?"

The cop says, "Sure, you can repeat what I say. But you have to stay close to me and be quiet. Do you understand?"

Sam says, "Yes, I understand. I will repeat what you say."

The cop says, "Okay, then. Let's go." He walks to the man and says, "Sir, please give me your license and registration."

Sam repeats, "Sir, please give me your license and registration."

The man looks at Sam and says, "What? Who are you?"

Sam says, "I am a cop too. I have a cop car. See?" He shows his toy cop car.

The man says, "You are not a cop. You are a kid. Go away."

Sam says, "No, I am a cop. I repeat what he says. He is a strong cop. He helps people and catches bad guys."

The man says, "You are a silly kid. You are not helping. You are annoying."

Sam says, "No, I am not silly. I am not annoying. I am a cop. I repeat what he says."

The cop says, "Okay, okay. That's enough. Sam, you are a very good cop. But you have to let me do my job. Why don't you go back to your house and play with your cop car there?"

Sam says, "Okay, okay. I will go back to my house. But can I come back and repeat what you say later?"

The cop says, "Maybe later. But only if you ask your mom or dad first. And only if you are very quiet and polite. Do you promise?"

Sam says, "I promise. I will ask my mom or dad first. And I will be very quiet and polite. Thank you, strong cop. You are very nice."

The cop says, "You are welcome, Sam. You are very brave and smart. Have fun with your cop car. Goodbye."

Sam says, "Goodbye, strong cop. Goodbye, angry man. I will see you later." He runs back to his house with his toy cop car. He is very happy. He likes to repeat what the cop says. He wants to be a strong cop when he grows up.

"Hello, bird," said Lila. "Can we see your eggs?"

The bird did not like Lila and Sam. It thought they were nosy and wanted to take its eggs. It made a loud noise and flapped its wings.

"Go away, go away," it said. "This is my nest. You are not welcome here."

The bird flew at Lila and Sam. It tried to strike them with its beak and claws. Lila and Sam were scared. They ducked and dodged. The bird tore Lila's blouse and scratched Sam's arm.

"Ow, ow, ow," they cried. "The bird is mean. Let's go down the tree."

They climbed down the tree as fast as they could. They ran to their mom, who was sitting on a bench. She saw their tears and wounds.

"What happened, my loves?" she asked. "Did you fall from the tree?"

"No, mom," said Lila. "A bird attacked us. It did not want us to see its nest."

"Oh, my poor babies," said mom. "You should not bother the bird. It was protecting its eggs. It was afraid of you. You should respect its home."

"I'm sorry, mom," said Sam. "We did not mean to make the bird angry. We just wanted to say hello."

Mom hugged them and kissed them. She gave them a band-aid and a cookie. She told them to be more careful and kind next time.

Lila and Sam learned their lesson. They decided to play on the swings instead. They looked at the tree and the bird from afar. They waved and said sorry. The bird calmed down and went back to its nest. It sang a song and smiled.

One night, Sara had a very bad dream. She dreamed that a huge white snake was chasing her in the forest. It had sharp teeth and red eyes. It hissed and slithered behind her. Sara ran and ran, but the snake was faster. She screamed for help, but no one heard her.

She woke up with a start. She was sweating and shaking. She felt like the snake was still there. She wanted to go to Mom and Dad, but her door was locked. She did not know how to unlock it. She was trapped in her room with her nightmare.

She cried and cried. She banged on the door. She called for Mom and Dad. She hoped they would hear her and come to save her.

Mom and Dad heard Sara's cries. They jumped out of bed and ran to her room. They saw that the door was locked. They did not know who locked it. They tried to open it, but it was stuck.

"Sara, honey, we're here. Don't be afraid. We'll get you out. Can you unlock the door?" Mom said.

"I don't know how. I'm scared. There's a snake in my dream. It wants to eat me." Sara said.

"It's okay, sweetie. It was just a dream. There's no snake. You're safe. We love you. We'll break the door if we have to." Dad said.

They pushed and pulled on the door. They heard a click. The door was unlocked. They opened it and saw Sara. She was crying and shaking. She ran to them and hugged them. They hugged her back and kissed her.

"Shh, shh, it's okay. You're okay. We're here. We're sorry the door was locked. We don't know how that happened. Do you want to sleep with us tonight?" Mom said.

"Yes, please. I don't want to sleep here. I don't like the dark. I don't like the snake." Sara said.

"Of course, honey. Come on, let's go to our bed. We'll keep you warm and safe. No more nightmares. We promise." Dad said.

They carried Sara to their bed. They tucked her in and cuddled with her. They sang her a lullaby and stroked her hair. Sara felt better. She felt loved. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She did not dream of the snake anymore. She dreamed of rainbows and butterflies. She smiled in her sleep.

Lily nodded and said: "OK, Ben, but we have to be careful. Don't lose the book or we can't grow back." They put the book on the floor and stood next to it. They held hands and said together: "Minus, minus, minus."

"What's this, mummy?" asked Billy.

"It's a present for you, Billy," said his mum. "Open it!"

Billy carefully pulled the ribbon and opened the box. Inside, he saw a shiny blue toy car. It was so tidy, he couldn't believe it!

"This is the best present ever!" said Billy as he zipped the toy car around the room. He was so happy that even the rain didn't bother him that day.

Dave wanted to cook something good. He opened his freezer to see what was inside. He saw some thick ice cream at the bottom. He was excited!

He said to himself, "This will make a delicious treat!" He grabbed the container of ice cream and some bowls.

He put the ice cream into the bowls and placed them in the kitchen. He grabbed a spoon and started stirring the ice cream.

When he was finished, the ice cream was thick and creamy. Dave said, "This looks and smells delicious!" He took a bite and smiled.

He said to his Mom who was in the kitchen with him, "Mom, I cooked something yummy. Do you want to try some?"

Mom said, "Of course! Let me have a spoonful."

They both enjoyed the thick and creamy ice cream. Dave said, "I'm so glad I used what I found in the freezer!"

One day, a young cat was lost in the big park. She could not find her mom or her home. She was very scared and sad. She cried and cried.

A kind dog saw the young cat crying. He came to her and said, "Why are you crying, little cat?"

The young cat said, "I am lost. I can't find my mom or my home. I don't know what to do."

The kind dog said, "Don't cry, little cat. I will help you. I will comfort you and we will look for your mom and your home together. Maybe they are near here. Come with me."

The young cat felt a little better. She said, "Thank you, kind dog. You are very nice to me. Can I be your friend?"

The kind dog said, "Of course, little cat. You can be my friend. Friends help each other. Come on, let's go."

The kind dog and the young cat walked around the park. They asked other animals if they knew where the young cat's mom and home were. They did not give up. They had to wait a long time, but they did not lose hope.

At last, they saw a house with a sign that said, "Cat's Home". The young cat recognized the sign. She said, "That's my home! That's where my mom is!"

The kind dog said, "I'm so happy for you, little cat. You found your home. Go and see your mom. She must be very worried about you."

The young cat said, "Thank you, kind dog. You are the best friend ever. You comforted me and helped me find my home. I will never forget you. Can I see you again?"

The kind dog said, "Yes, little cat. You can see me again. I live in the park. I will come and visit you sometimes. And you can come and play with me too. Goodbye, little cat. Be happy and safe."

The young cat ran to her home. She saw her mom waiting for her. She hugged her mom and told her everything. Her mom was very glad and thankful. She said, "You are very brave, little cat. And you are very lucky to have such a kind friend. Always be kind to others, like the kind dog was to you. Kindness is the best gift you can give and receive."

The young cat nodded. She learned a valuable lesson. She was happy and grateful. She looked at the park and waved to the kind dog. He waved back and smiled. They were friends forever. The end.

"Wow!" Sara said. "What is that?"

Ben came over and looked at the ball too. He was amazed. He touched the ball and felt something hard and smooth.

"It's not a bug," he said. "It's a ball."

They wondered what was inside the ball. They waited and watched.

After a while, the ball began to crack. A small hole appeared on the ball. Sara and Ben leaned closer. They saw a flash of color. Something came out of the hole. It was a butterfly!

The butterfly was beautiful. It had wings of blue and purple and pink. It looked happy and free. It flew out of the ball and landed on Sara's nose.

"Hello, butterfly!" Sara said. "You are so pretty!"

The butterfly fluttered its wings and tickled Sara's nose. She giggled.

"Hello, Sara!" the butterfly said. "You are so kind!"

Sara and Ben were surprised. They did not know the butterfly could talk.

"Who are you?" Ben asked.

The butterfly smiled and said, "I am the caterpillar. I was in the ball. I changed into a butterfly."

Sara and Ben were shocked. They did not know the caterpillar could change into a butterfly.

"Wow!" they said. "You are amazing!"

The butterfly thanked them and said, "I'm sorry I bit you, Ben. I was scared and hungry. But you were nice to me. You did not hurt me. You let me stay in the flower. You helped me become a butterfly."

Ben forgave the butterfly and said, "It's okay. I'm glad you are happy now. You are a good friend."

The butterfly hugged Sara and Ben and said, "You are good friends too. I have to go now. I have to see the world. But I will always remember you. Goodbye!"

The butterfly flew away and disappeared in the sky. Sara and Ben waved goodbye and smiled. They learned a new thing. They learned that sometimes things change. And sometimes things that seem bad can become good. And sometimes things that seem good can become better. They were happy. They went to play in the garden. They hoped to see the butterfly again.

Ben hugged Lily and said, "Lily, Lily, I'm glad you are okay. You are still my best friend. You are brave and strong. You will be fine."

They hugged each other and felt better. They saw a lady coming to help them. She was a nurse. She said, "Hello, children. I saw what happened. You had a bad fall. But don't worry, I will take care of you. I will clean your wound and put a bandage on it. I will give you some ice for your bump. You will feel better soon."

Lily and Ben thanked the nurse. They felt grateful and relieved. They said, "Thank you, nurse. You are kind and helpful. You are a good person."

The nurse smiled and said, "You're welcome, children. You are very sweet and polite. You are good friends. You should be proud of yourselves."

Lily and Ben smiled and said, "We are, nurse. We are proud of ourselves. And we are proud of each other."

Lily was a pupil in a big school. She liked to learn new things and play with her friends. But she did not like to wear a white dress every day. She thought it was boring and dirty.

One day, she decided to complain to her teacher. She said, "Teacher, why do we have to wear white dresses? They are not fun and they get stained. Can we wear other colors?"

The teacher smiled and said, "Lily, I understand how you feel. But the white dress is part of our school uniform. It shows that we are all the same and we respect each other. It also helps us to look neat and tidy. Do you see?"

Lily nodded, but she was not convinced. She still wanted to wear other colors. She thought of a plan. She asked her mom to buy her some colorful stickers. She put them on her white dress and made it look like a rainbow.

The next day, she went to school with her new dress. She was very happy and proud. She showed it to her friends and they liked it too. But the teacher was not happy. She said, "Lily, what have you done to your dress? You have ruined it. You have to take off those stickers and wear a clean white dress. This is not acceptable."

Lily was sad and angry. She did not want to take off her stickers. She said, "But teacher, I like my dress. It is fun and pretty. It shows that I am different and I have a personality. Why can't I wear it?"

The teacher sighed and said, "Lily, I appreciate your creativity and your individuality. But you have to follow the rules of the school. The white dress is not just a dress. It is a symbol of our values and our identity. It is important that you respect that. Do you understand?"

Lily looked at her teacher and saw that she was serious and kind. She realized that she had made a mistake. She said, "I'm sorry, teacher. I understand. I will take off my stickers and wear a clean white dress. But can I keep them in my bag and use them for other things?"

The teacher nodded and said, "Of course, Lily. You can use your stickers for your art projects or your notebooks. But not for your dress. Thank you for being honest and cooperative. I'm proud of you."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, teacher. I'm sorry for complaining. I will try to be a good pupil and wear my white dress. But can I still wear my pink shoes?"

The teacher laughed and said, "Yes, Lily. You can still wear your pink shoes. They are very cute and they match your stickers. Now, let's go to the classroom and learn something new."

Lily and the teacher walked to the classroom, holding hands. Lily was happy and learned to appreciate her white dress. She also learned to respect the teacher and the school. She still liked to wear other colors, but she knew when and where to wear them. She was a smart and creative pupil.

Lily was a dog who liked to play with her friends. She was good at running, jumping and catching balls. She was also very friendly and polite. She always said hello and goodbye to other dogs and people. She knew how to bow, which was a way of showing respect and kindness.

One day, she met a new dog in the park. His name was Max and he was big and fluffy. He had a red collar and a shiny tag. Lily wanted to be his friend, so she ran up to him and bowed. She said, "Hi, I'm Lily. Do you want to play with me?"

Max looked at her and snorted. He did not bow back. He said, "No, I don't want to play with you. You are too small and plain. You don't have a collar or a tag. You are not important. Go away."

Lily felt sad and hurt. She did not understand why Max was so mean. She walked away and found her old friends. They were happy to see her and invited her to join their game. They said, "Lily, you are a great friend. You are fun and nice. You are important to us."

Lily smiled and thanked them. She played with them and had a good time. She forgot about Max and his rude words.

Later, she saw Max again. He was scratching his fur with his paws. He looked unhappy and annoyed. He had a big itch that he could not reach. He tried to rub against a tree, but it did not help. He tried to bite his fur, but it hurt. He tried to ask other dogs for help, but they ignored him. They remembered how he had treated Lily and did not want to be his friend.

Lily saw him and felt sorry for him. She remembered how he had made her feel, but she also remembered how to be kind. She decided to help him. She walked up to him and said, "Hi, Max. I see you have an itch. Do you want me to scratch it for you?"

Max was surprised and ashamed. He said, "Why would you help me? I was mean to you. I said you were not important. I don't deserve your help."

Lily said, "It's okay, Max. Everyone makes mistakes. You can still be a good dog. You just need to learn how to bow and be nice to others. They are important too. Here, let me scratch your itch."

She scratched his itch with her teeth and tongue. Max felt relieved and grateful. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind and generous. You are a good friend. I'm sorry for what I said. You are important to me."

Lily said, "You're welcome, Max. I'm glad you feel better. Do you want to play with me and my friends?"

Max said, "Yes, I do. I would love to play with you and your friends. Can you teach me how to bow?"

Lily said, "Of course, I can. It's easy and fun. Come on, let's go."

They ran to join the other dogs. Max bowed to them and said hello. They welcomed him and invited him to join their game. They all played happily and became friends.

The moral of the story is: Be kind and polite to others, even if they are different from you. You never know when you might need their help or friendship. Bowing is a way of showing respect and kindness. Everyone is important and deserves to be treated well.

They take the box to the middle of the room. They cut a door and a window with scissors. They draw some wheels and a flag with crayons. They rub some glue and stick some stickers on the box. They make it look very nice.

"Wow, it is a great box!" Sara says. "Can I go inside first?"

"No, I go first!" Ben says. "I made it more than you!"

"Stop, stop!" Mom says. She comes into the room. She sees the mess and the broken box. She is very sad and angry. "What did you do to the box? Why did you fight over it?"

"Sorry, Mom," Sara and Ben say. They feel very sorry and ashamed. "We wanted to play with the box, but we could not share it."

Mom sighs. She picks up the box and puts it in the trash. She takes Sara and Ben to the stand. The stand has many books and games and puzzles. They are for children who have no toys.

"Look at these children," Mom says. "They have nothing to play with. They would be very happy to have a box like yours. But you wasted it and ruined it. You should be more grateful and kind."

Sara and Ben look at the children. They see their smiles and their eyes. They feel very bad and sorry. They wish they could give them the box.

"Mom, we are sorry," Sara and Ben say. "We were selfish and mean. We did not think of others. We want to help these children. Can we give them some of our toys?"

Mom smiles. She hugs Sara and Ben. She is very proud and happy. "Yes, you can," she says. "That is very generous and nice of you. You learned a good lesson today. Sharing is caring."

Sara and Ben take some of their toys and give them to the children. The children are very happy and thankful. They play with the toys and share them. Sara and Ben play with them too. They make new friends and have fun. They forget about the box. They are glad they shared.

Sara takes out Bob from her pocket. She holds him in her hand. She says, "This is Bob. He is my potato friend. I made him a face. Do you like him?" Lily looks at Bob. She sees his eyes, nose and mouth. She thinks he is funny. She says, "He is cute. Can I hold him?" Sara says, "Yes, you can. But be careful. He is fragile."

Lily holds Bob gently. She smiles at him. She says, "Hello, Bob. You are a nice potato. Do you want to play with us?" Bob does not answer. He is a potato. He cannot talk. But Sara and Lily pretend he can. They make him talk with funny voices. They make him dance and sing. They have a lot of fun with Bob. They are good friends. They love potatoes.

Tom nodded and ran to the bush. He reached for a berry, but Sara stopped him. She said, "Wait, Tom, not that one. That one is spoil. It is soft and brown. It will make you sick. Pick a good one. A good one is hard and bright."

Tom looked at the berry. He saw that it was spoil. He dropped it and picked another one. He said, "Thank you, Sara. You are smart. How do you know which berry is good and which is spoil?"

Sara smiled and said, "Mommy taught me. She said we have to be careful with berries. Some are good and some are spoil. Some are even bad. Bad berries are not red. They are other colors. They can hurt you. We have to leave them alone."

Tom nodded and said, "I see. Mommy is smart too. Can we eat the good berries now?"

Sara said, "Yes, we can. But not too many. We have to share with Mommy and Daddy. They will like the berries too. And we have to wash them first. There are bugs and dirt on them. Come on, let's go to the kitchen. There is water available."

Lila was a little girl who loved to look at the stars. Every night, she would go outside with her dad and point at the bright dots in the sky. She wanted to learn their names and stories.

One night, her dad said, "Look, Lila, there is something special in the sky. It is a comet. A comet is a ball of ice and dust that goes very fast around the sun. Sometimes, we can see it when it comes close to the earth. It has a long tail that shines like a firework."

Lila was amazed by the comet. She thought it was the most beautiful thing she had ever seen. She asked her dad, "Can we keep the comet? Can we take it home and put it in a jar?"

Her dad smiled and shook his head. "No, Lila, we cannot keep the comet. The comet belongs to the sky. It is not ours to take. We can only watch it and enjoy it for a little while. That is what makes it special. We value it because it is rare and wonderful."

Lila felt sad. She wanted to have the comet as her own. She thought it would make her happy. She said, "But I love the comet. I don't want it to go away. I want it to stay with me forever."

Her dad hugged her and said, "I know, Lila, I know. But you cannot love something by keeping it for yourself. You have to let it be free and do what it is meant to do. The comet has a journey to make. It has to explore the space and visit other planets. Maybe one day, it will come back and we will see it again. But until then, we have to say goodbye and thank it for the joy it gave us."

Lila looked at the comet again. She saw that it was getting smaller and fainter. She felt a tear roll down her cheek. She said, "Goodbye, comet. Thank you for being so pretty. I hope you have fun in the space. I will miss you."

Her dad kissed her and said, "You are a very brave and kind girl, Lila. I am proud of you. You have learned a valuable lesson today. Sometimes, the things that make us happy are not the things that we can have, but the things that we can share. Come on, let's go inside. It is getting cold and dark. We can read a book or play a game. I love you, Lila."

Lila nodded and smiled. She felt a little better. She still loved the comet, but she also loved her dad. She realized that he was right. The comet was not hers, but it was a gift. Anna held Lily's hand and said, "What is the magic word?"

Lily said, "It is 'reveal'."

Anna repeated, "Reveal!"

Suddenly, the mirror glowed and showed them a new scene. They saw a castle, a garden and a unicorn. Anna and Lily were amazed and said, "Wow!"

"Come on, tiger, let's see what's in there!" he said to his toy. He held it in his arms and walked into the cave. It was dark and cold and he could hear strange noises. He felt scared, but he wanted to be brave like a tiger.

He walked deeper and deeper into the cave, until he saw a bright light at the end. He ran towards it, hoping to find a way out. But when he reached the light, he realized it was not an exit, but a hole in the ceiling. He looked up and saw a huge bird with sharp claws and a long beak. It was an eagle, and it was hungry.

The eagle saw Tom and his tiger and swooped down to grab them. Tom screamed and tried to run away, but it was too late. The eagle caught them in its talons and flew away. Tom dropped his tiger as he was lifted into the air. He watched as his tiger fell to the ground and disappeared among the rocks.

The tiger was angry that someone had taken his cub, and he climbed up the tree to the nest. He fought with the eagle and scared it away. He then saw Tom, who was trembling and crying. Tom was amazed and grateful. He hugged his tiger and thanked the real tiger. He said he was sorry for pretending to be a tiger and for going into the cave. He said he learned his lesson and he would never do it again. He asked the real tiger to take him home.

The end.

One day, a fisherman went to the lake to catch some fish. He had a big net and a small boat. He put the net in the water and waited for the fish to swim in.

Soon, he felt a tug on the net. He pulled hard, but the net was very heavy. He saw a huge fish in the net. It was bigger than his boat. The fisherman was scared and happy. He wanted to take the fish home, but he did not know how.

He tried to lift the net, but it was too hard. He tried to push the fish, but it was too strong. He tried to call for help, but no one heard him. He did not know what to do.

Then, he had an idea. He took a bucket and filled it with water. He poured the water on the fish. He did it again and again. He hoped the fish would like the water and calm down.

The fish felt the water on its skin. It liked the water. It stopped thrashing and looked at the fisherman. The fisherman smiled and said, "Hello, fish. I am sorry I caught you. You are very beautiful and amazing. Do you want to go back to the lake?"

The fish nodded and made a sound. It thanked the fisherman for the water and said, "Yes, please. I want to go back to the lake. I have a family and friends there. You are very kind and brave. Can we be friends?"

The fisherman nodded and made a sound. He said, "Yes, of course. We can be friends. I will let you go. But can I visit you sometimes?"

The fish agreed and said, "Yes, you can. I will wait for you in the lake. But please, do not bring your net. Just bring your bucket and some water."

The fisherman agreed and said, "OK, I will. Goodbye, fish. Take care."

He cut the net and freed the fish. The fish swam away, but turned back and waved. The fisherman waved back and rowed his boat to the shore. He was happy and proud. He had a new friend. He had a huge fish.

Her parent smiled and said it was a comet, a rare kind of star that travels very fast and only comes once in a long time.

Lily was amazed and curious. She wanted to know more about the comet, where it came from, where it was going, and why it had a tail. Her parent explained that the comet was made of ice and dust, and that it came from far away, beyond the other stars. It was going around the sun, which made it shine and melt, and that was why it had a tail. The tail always pointed away from the sun, because of the wind in space.

Lily thought the comet was very beautiful and special. She wished she could see it again, but her parent told her that it would soon be gone, and that they were lucky to see it at all. Lily felt a little sad, but also happy that she had shared this rare sight with her parent. She hugged her parent and thanked them for telling her about the comet. One day, she went to the park with her mother. She saw a boy who was playing with a ball near a well. The ball was old and dirty, and the boy had no other toys. Lily felt sorry for the boy, but she did not want to give him any of her toys. She thought that he would ruin them or lose them.

She decided to play with her doll near the well. She pretended that her doll was a princess who lived in a castle. She made up stories about her doll and her castle, and did not notice the boy who was watching her.

The boy was curious about the doll. He wanted to see it and touch it. He thought that the doll was very pretty and looked like a real princess. He walked up to Lily and said, "Hello, can I play with your doll?"

Lily was surprised and angry. She did not like the boy who came near her. She said, "No, you can't play with my doll. She is mine and she is very expensive. You have a dirty ball and you are poor. Go away and leave me alone."

The boy felt sad and hurt. He did not understand why Lily was so mean to him. He said, "I'm sorry, I just wanted to be your friend. I don't have any other toys or friends. Your doll is very nice and I like her. Please, can I play with her for a little while?"

Lily did not listen to the boy. She turned away from him and hugged her doll. She said, "No, no, no. You can't be my friend. You can't play with my doll. She is only for me. Go away and don't bother me."

The boy felt very lonely and rejected. He walked away from Lily and went back to his ball. He kicked his ball hard and it flew into the air. He watched it as it went higher and higher, until it fell into the well.

He ran to the well and looked down. He saw his ball sinking into the water. He cried and cried. He had lost his only toy and his only friend.

Lily heard the boy crying and looked at him. She saw him standing by the well, with tears in his eyes. She felt a pang of guilt and pity. She realized that she had been very selfish and rude. She thought that maybe she could share her doll with the boy and make him happy. She thought that maybe he could be her friend and play with her.

Lily smiled and handed her doll to the boy. They sat down by the well and played with the doll. They made up stories and laughed. They forgot about the ball and the well. They became friends and shared their toys and clothes.

The moral of the story is: It is better to share and accept than to be selfish and reject. You can find happiness and friendship in simple things. You can be wealthy in your heart, not in your things.

His curiosity made him too eager and he stepped closer to the pot. Suddenly, he felt a sharp pain in his foot. He had stepped on something sharp! Tim felt hurt and quickly stepped back.

However, he was surprised to see that the pot of steaming hot sauce had a label on the side. It read "Mama's special hurt sauce!" Tim realized by touching the hot sauce, he would have felt much less hurt than he had. He thanked his lucky stars and stepped away from the pot. 

The next time Tim was exploring, he kept an eye out for Mama's special hurt sauce. He knew if he ever stepped on something sharp again, he could always trust in that special sauce to help him feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a lively little dog named Fido. He loved to play and run in the park. One day, while Fido was playing, he came across a curious oat. He looked at it, sniffed it and quickly ate it all up. 

Fido's owner, Mrs. Smith, saw him and quickly called him over. She said, "Fido, why did you eat that oat?" 

Fido hung his head in shame and replied, "I didn't know, Mrs. Smith". 

Mrs. Smith kneeled down and looked him in the eyes, "I want you to remember, Fido, that when something doesn't belong to you, it's best to leave it alone. Unauthorized release of someone else's belongings can be very bad". 

Fido nodded, understanding the important lesson Mrs. Smith was teaching him. From that day on, he never touched another oat that didn't belong to him and stayed lively while playing in the park. 

The moral of the story is that when it comes to someone else's belongings, it's best to leave it alone.

After they finished playing, Lily said, "I collected some pretty flowers today, do you want to see?" Max said, "Yes, I love flowers!" They went to Lily's garden and Max was amazed by all the beautiful flowers she had collected. He was glad he played with Lily and made a new friend.

Lily played with the pistol and ran around the farm. But then she started to feel dizzy. "I don't feel good," she said to her grandpa. "Let's go inside and rest," he replied.

Ant said, "Yes, I do. But is it safe? What if the bees are angry?"

Bee said, "Don't worry. They are nice to me. Come, I will show you."

They flew and crawled to the hive. Bee said hello to the other bees. They let him and Ant in. The hive was warm and sweet. Ant saw many cells with honey and wax. He said, "Wow, this is amazing. Can I have some honey?"

Bee said, "Sure, you can. But only a little. We need honey for winter. And be careful. Some cells have baby bees. They are very small and soft. Do not touch them."

Ant nodded. He found a cell with honey. He licked it. It was delicious. He wanted more. He looked for another cell. He saw one that was red. He thought it was honey. He poked it with his antenna.

But it was not honey. It was a flower. A bee had brought it to feed a baby bee. The flower was red because it had a sting. The sting hurt Ant. He cried, "Ow, ow, ow! Help, help, help!"

The bees heard him. They were angry. They thought he was a thief. They said, "Who are you? Why are you here? What did you do?"

Bee said, "He is my friend. He is Ant. He did not know. He was curious. Please, do not hurt him."

But the bees did not listen. They buzzed and chased Ant. They wanted to sting him. Ant was scared. He said, "Bee, help me. How can I escape?"

Bee said, "Follow me. I know a way out. Hurry, hurry, hurry!"

They ran and flew to the exit. The bees followed them. They were close. Ant and Bee saw the sun. They were almost free. But then, a big bird saw them. The bird was hungry. It opened its beak. It wanted to eat them.

Ant and Bee were in trouble. They had to escape from the bees and the bird. They did not know what to do. They said, "Oh, no, oh, no, oh, no!"

But then, they saw a flower. The flower was big and yellow. It had a hole. They said, "Look, a flower. Maybe we can hide there."

They flew and crawled to the flower. They went inside the hole. The flower was soft and nice. It smelled good. They felt safe. The bees and the bird did not see them. They went away.

Ant and Bee sighed. They were happy. They had escaped. They said, "Phew, that was close. Thank you, flower. Thank you, Bee. You saved me."

Bee said, "You are welcome, Ant. You are my friend. But next time, be careful. Do not touch what you do not know. And do not take what is not yours. It can be dangerous."

Ant said, "I am sorry, Bee. I was greedy and foolish. I learned my lesson. I will not do it again. I will respect your home and your family. And I will share what I have with you."

Bee said, "That is good, Ant. I am glad you are sorry. I forgive you. And I will share what I have with you, too. We are friends. We help each other. We are happy."

Lily and Tom nodded and started to cut the lettuce. Lily was very careful and cut small pieces. Tom wanted to finish faster and cut big pieces. He saw that the knife was huge and shiny and thought it was fun to swing it around.

"Look, Lily, I can make the knife fly!" Tom said and threw the knife in the air.

"Tom, no, that is dangerous!" Lily shouted and ducked.

The knife flew over Lily's head and landed on the table. It made a loud noise and cut the cheese in half. Mom heard the noise and came to see what happened.

"Tom, what did you do?" mom asked, very angry. "You could have hurt yourself or Lily or me! You did not listen to me and you did not use the knife properly. You are not allowed to use the knife anymore. Go to your room and think about what you did."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches that knives are not toys and that we have to use them carefully and responsibly. It also teaches that we have to listen to our parents and that we can forgive and make up with our siblings.

Lily ran as fast as she could and finally reached home. She showed her mom the feathers and told her about the noisy duck. From that day on, Lily never tried to collect feathers from the ducks again.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the woods. They would run, jump, climb and explore. One day, they saw a big nest on a high tree. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's pick some twigs and make a ladder," Tom said. He was gifted at making things. "Then we can climb up and look at the nest."

"OK," Sam said. He followed Tom and helped him pick some twigs. They tied them together with vines and leaned them against the tree. Tom went first and climbed up the ladder. Sam waited below.

Tom reached the nest and peeked inside. He saw four eggs that were blue and speckled. He thought they were pretty and wanted to touch them. He reached out his hand and touched one of the eggs. It was warm and smooth.

Suddenly, he heard a loud screech. He looked up and saw a big bird flying towards him. It was angry and had sharp claws and a long beak. It was the mother of the eggs. Tom was scared and tried to climb down the ladder. But the bird was faster and attacked him. It scratched his face and bit his arm. Tom screamed and fell off the ladder.

Sam heard Tom scream and saw him fall. He ran to him and saw that he was hurt and bleeding. He cried and called for help. The bird flew away with her eggs.

The moral of the story is: Do not touch what does not belong to you. You might get hurt or make someone angry.

"Oh, no. That's a big problem. You need shoes to go outside. Maybe you can borrow your sister's shoes. Or maybe you can ask your mom to help you look for them," Mia said.

"Good idea, Mia. I will try that. I will call you back when I find them. Bye," Lily said.

Mia hung up the phone and went back to the kitchen. She told her mom what Lily said.

"Don't worry, Mia. I'm sure Lily will find her shoes soon. The cake is almost ready. Let's put some sprinkles on top. That will make it more fun," her mom said.

Mia smiled and grabbed a handful of sprinkles. She sprinkled them all over the cake. She made a pattern of stars and hearts. She was proud of her work.

"Wow, Mia. You are very creative. The cake looks beautiful. I think Lily will love it," her mom said.

"Thank you, mom. I love you. And I love Lily. She is my friend. I hope she finds her shoes," Mia said.

The end.

One day, Tim and Sam are playing in the yard. Tim has a red car and Sam has a blue car. They race their cars on the grass. Tim's car is faster than Sam's car. Tim wins the race. He is happy. He says, "I am the best! My car is the best! Your car is slow and bad!"

Sam is sad and angry. He says, "No, you are not the best! You are mean and rude! I hate you! I hate your car!" He throws his car at Tim. The car hits Tim on the head. Tim cries. He says, "Ow! That hurts! You are a bad brother! I hate you too!"

Tim and Sam nod. They are alert. They do not want to lose their cars or break them. They love their cars. They love each other. They follow Mom to the house. They are happy. They do not fight anymore.

Lily was scared. She did not know what to say. She held her scarf tight.

Her mom said, "Lily, Ben is nice. He wants to be your friend. You can share your scarf and play with his truck. It will be fun."

Lily and Ben were playing in the yard. They liked to find rocks and measure them with a ruler. Lily had a big rock that was ten inches long. Ben had a small rock that was only four inches long.

"Look at my rock, Lily. It is so big and shiny!" Lily said. She was proud of her rock.

"My rock is better, Ben. It is smooth and round. And it is sweet!" Ben said. He licked his rock and smiled.

"Sweet? Rocks are not sweet, Ben. They are hard and dirty. You are silly!" Lily said. She did not believe Ben.

"Yes, they are! Try it, Lily. It is like candy!" Ben said. He held out his rock to Lily.

Lily was curious. She took Ben's rock and put it in her mouth. But it was not sweet at all. It was sour and bitter. Lily spit out the rock and made a face.

"Yuck! This is not candy, Ben. This is a lemon!" Lily said. She was angry at Ben.

"Oops! I made a mistake, Lily. I'm sorry. I thought it was a rock. It looks like a rock, see?" Ben said. He showed Lily the lemon. It was yellow and had bumps like a rock.

Lily looked at the lemon. She saw that it was not a rock. She felt sorry for Ben. He did not know the difference.

"It's okay, Ben. You did not mean to trick me. But lemons are not rocks. They are fruits. They are good for making juice, not for measuring." Lily said. She gave Ben a hug.

"Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. Can we still play with rocks?" Ben said. He smiled at Lily.

"Of course, Ben. But let's find real rocks, not lemons. And let's share them, too. Maybe we can find a sweet rock together." Lily said. She smiled back at Ben.

They put the lemon aside and went to look for more rocks. They had fun measuring them and comparing them. They were happy.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to dig and find things. Sometimes they found worms, sometimes they found stones, sometimes they found nothing.

One day, they found something shiny and hard. It was round and had a hole in the middle. Lily picked it up and showed it to Tom.

"Look, what is this?" she asked.

"I don't know, maybe a ring?" Tom guessed.

"Can I wear it?" Lily wondered.

"Sure, try it on. Maybe it is a fancy ring for a princess," Tom said.

Lily put the ring on her finger. It was too big, but she liked it. She felt very fancy.

She ran to show her mom. She saw her mom in the kitchen, cooking something on the stove. There was fire under the pot.

"Mom, mom, look what I found!" Lily shouted.

She waved her hand with the ring. But the ring was not just shiny and hard. It was also sparky and hot. It made a loud noise and a bright flash. The fire under the pot jumped up and touched the ring.

"Ouch!" Lily cried. She dropped the ring on the floor. It made another noise and another flash.

"Fire, fire!" Tom yelled. He ran to get some water.

Mom turned off the stove and grabbed a towel. She put out the fire on the ring and on the pot. She checked Lily's hand. It was red and sore, but not burned.

"Lily, Tom, are you okay?" Mom asked.

"Yes, Mom, we are okay. But what was that?" Lily asked.

"That was not a ring, my dear. That was a firework. A firework is something that makes fire and noise and light in the sky. It is for special days, not for playing. Where did you find it?" Mom explained.

"We found it in the garden. We thought it was a fancy ring," Tom said.

"Well, you were very lucky. Fireworks are dangerous. They can hurt you and start fires. You should never touch them or play with them. If you find something like that again, you should tell me or Dad right away. Do you understand?" Mom said.

"Yes, Mom, we understand. We are sorry. We didn't know," Lily and Tom said.

Mom hugged them and kissed their heads. She put some cream on Lily's hand and gave them some cookies.

"Next time, be more careful. And don't worry, you are still my fancy princess and my brave prince," Mom said.

When night time came, the bird rested in a tree. He heard a loud noise and saw a bright light. When he looked down, he saw a kind old man. The man asked the bird, "What are you doing so far away from home?"

The bird replied, "I want to find wisdom and escape from my everyday." The old man smiled, "Wisdom is within you, it is not out here." The bird looked deep within himself and saw that it was true. He thanked the old man and flew away to his home where he shared his wisdom with his friends and family.

When they arrived, Jem was so excited! He looked out to sea and saw a big cabin far away. He wanted to go explore it!

Jem's mum said "No, Jem. We can't swim that far and the cabin looks very old. You wouldn't want to get stuck there."

Jem was ignorant of the danger and he splashed into the sea. His mum was scared so she shouted out to him, "Jem, get back here now!"

Jem turned and saw the fear in his mum's eyes. He slowly paddled back, feeling sad but also proud of his bravery, even though he hadn't managed to reach the cabin.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle worm. He loved to explore the world around him. One day, he came upon a big rock. He was curious to split it open and see what was inside.

As he peered inside, something caught his eye. It was a beautiful butterfly. He could see its wings spread wide and its colorful patterns.

The butterfly spoke: "Thank you for setting me free, little worm. You are gentle and strong." The worm was so happy to hear this.

The worm smiled and thought, "Maybe I'm a hero, after all." Then, he continued on his adventure.

The bird smiled and said, "You're welcome. It's my pleasure to help."

Finally, the snowman made it to the top of the hill. But no sooner had he made it, than a strong gust of strong wind blew around him and started to push him backwards. He struggled to stay put, and he held on tightly to his hat. 

The wind grew stronger and stronger and it kept pushing the snowman from side to side. But he kept on struggling, refusing to give up.

Finally, the wind subsided and the snowman stayed put. He was exhausted and had to sit down, but he was so happy that he had made it. He had now seen the most amazing view at the top of the hill and he had struggled against the wind to get there. He was definitely proud of himself!

Tommy kept walking and soon he noticed another mosquito buzzing around his ears. He said "thank you" again and then ran back to his house. He sprayed himself with insect repellent and said "thank you" one more time.

Tommy was safe from the scary mosquitos and adventure in the woods could continue. 

The end!

Suddenly, Bitey heard a friendly voice say, "Oh Bitey, why are you biting the top?" 

Bitey thought for a moment and then answered, "Because I want to play with it!" 

The voice said, "Well, you can play with it, but not by biting it. Take a look and find different ways to play. Try spinning it, rolling it, and flipping it."

Bitey was excited and tried all the different ways to play. He spun it around, rolled it, and flipped it. It was so much fun!

Bitey had a wonderful time, and the top was still in one piece when he was done. Bitey had learned a lesson: playing with the top was a much better way to have fun, than biting it.

The end.

After the delivery, Spot went back home and took a nap in the sun. He dreamed of all the other things he could deliver to help his neighbors. From that day on, Spot always looked for ways to be helpful and make others happy.

The next day, the girl went back to play the piano, but she couldn't find her little brother anywhere. She looked and looked, but he was nowhere to be found. She asked her parents where he was, but they didn't know either. 

Days turned into weeks and weeks turned into months, but the little brother never came back. The girl realized that her anger and frustration had caused her to say something hurtful to her brother that day. She regretted it deeply, but it was too late. She never saw her brother again and her heart was forever heavy with sadness.

Timmy learned a lesson that day. He realized that even though he really wanted to touch the puppy, it wasn't safe. From then on, he listened to his mom and didn't try to touch animals without permission.

Once upon a time, there was a big cow who lived in a field. The cow was very wild and liked to run around and play. One day, the cow saw a big truck drive by and it got very excited. The truck was going to the park and the cow wanted to go too.

The cow ran after the truck and followed it to the park. When it got there, the cow saw lots of other animals playing and having fun. The cow wanted to join in, but it was too wild and scared the other animals away.

As the sun started to set, the cow realized it was getting late and it needed to go home. But it didn't know the way back to the field. The cow got lost and couldn't find its way back. It was very scared and alone in the dark.

The next day, the farmer found the cow lying in the park. The cow had been attacked by a wild animal and had died. The farmer was very sad and wished the cow had stayed in the field where it was safe.

Her mom replied, "We'll see, Lily. It depends on how long the store takes. We have to yield to the other people in the store, and sometimes it takes a while."

When they got to the store, Lily saw that there were a lot of toys available. She asked her mom if she could get one, but her mom said they didn't have enough money.

Lily was sad, but her mom told her they could still have fun at the park. And after they finished shopping, they went to the park and played on the swings and the slide. It was a fun morning for Lily and her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to eat candy all day long, but she never polished her teeth. One day, Lily's mom told her that she needed to start polishing her teeth or they would turn yellow and hurt. Lily didn't listen to her mom and kept eating candy.

One day, Lily's mouth started to hurt really bad. She went to the dentist and he told her that she had cavities. The dentist had to clean her teeth and it was very painful. Lily learned her lesson and started to polish her teeth every day.

The moral of the story is that it's important to take care of your teeth by polishing them. If you don't, your mouth will hurt and you will have to go to the dentist. So always keep your mouth busy by polishing your teeth!

When they got to the mechanic, Max saw a pretty lady working there. He thought she was very attractive. Max's mom talked to the mechanic and explained the problem with the car. The mechanic said, "Don't worry, I can fix it for you." Max watched as the mechanic worked on his car.

Suddenly, Max heard a loud scream. He turned around and saw a dog barking at a cat. Max laughed and said, "Look, the dog is screaming!" His mom smiled and said, "Yes, he is." Finally, the mechanic fixed Max's car and Max was happy again. He thanked the mechanic and the pretty lady and went home to play with his newly fixed car.

Lily felt sad that they couldn't catch the butterfly. "Don't worry, Lily. We can try again tomorrow," said Max, who always knew how to make Lily feel better. Lily smiled and hugged Max, grateful for her obedient and caring friend.

Later, Tim's mom came outside and saw the hole. She asked Tim what he did. Tim told her about the sugar. His mom laughed and said, "Oh, you silly boy! Sugar is for eating, not for burying!" Tim smiled and promised not to bury sugar again.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a toy that he loved a lot. The toy had a switch on it. When Tim turned the switch, the toy would make a funny sound. Tim liked to play with the toy every day. He would care for the toy and make sure it was always clean and safe.

One day, Tim took his toy to school. He wanted to show it to his friends. At lunch time, Tim turned the switch on the toy. The toy made its funny sound. But instead of laughing, his friends looked at him. Tim felt embarrassed. He did not know why his friends did not think the toy was funny.

After school, Tim told his mom what happened. His mom hugged him and said, "It's okay to feel embarrassed. But remember, you love your toy and you care for it. That's what matters most." Tim smiled and felt better. He knew that even if his friends did not like his toy, he still cared for it and that was enough.

Once upon a time, in a big green garden, there was a curious little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside and look at all the things around him. One sunny day, Tim saw a tiny insect moving on the ground. He was very excited and wanted to watch the insect.

As the insect moved, Tim followed it. The insect was a little ant, and it was carrying a big leaf. Tim was curious about where the ant was going. He saw that the ant was moving to a small hill with lots of other ants. They were all working together to build their home.

Tim learned that when we work together, we can do big things. The moral of the story is that teamwork makes everything easier and better. From that day on, Tim always tried to help his friends and family, just like the ants.

Once upon a time, in a wild forest, there lived a little crane. The crane was very friendly and loved to play with all the animals. One day, the crane met a small squirrel who was scared of the big trees.

"Hello, squirrel. Why are you scared?" asked the crane. The squirrel looked up and said, "I want to go to the top of the tree, but I don't trust myself. I am too small, and the tree is too big."

The crane smiled and said, "Don't worry, squirrel. I can help you. Trust me, I will take you to the top of the tree." The squirrel was happy and climbed onto the crane's back. The crane flew up and up, and soon they reached the top of the tree.

The squirrel was so happy and thanked the crane. They became the best of friends and played together every day. The squirrel learned to trust the crane, and the crane taught the squirrel how to be brave in the wild forest.

From that day on, all the animals in the forest knew they could trust the friendly crane. They all lived happily together, playing and helping each other in the wild forest.

Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there lived a very intelligent rabbit named Remy. Remy was always hopping around and playing with his friends. One day, Remy and his friends decided to play a fun game of "Guess the Motion."

"Let's take turns and guess each other's motion," said Remy. His friends nodded and agreed. First up was Remy's best friend, Benny the squirrel. Benny started to move his arms and legs in a funny way. Remy giggled and said, "I guess you are swimming!" Benny smiled and said, "Yes, you are right!"

Next, it was Remy's turn to make a motion. He stood up on his back legs and started to hop in a circle. Benny and the other friends laughed and tried to guess. "Are you dancing?" asked Benny. Remy shook his head and said, "No, try again!" After a few more tries, Benny finally guessed, "You are spinning like a top!" Remy clapped his paws and said, "Yes, you got it!"

Remy and his friends played "Guess the Motion" all day long. They had so much fun and learned that they could be very intelligent by using their minds to guess each other's motions. As the sun began to set, they all went back to their homes in the big green forest, excited to play the game again another day.

Tommy liked to watch the flies in the garden. They buzzed and zoomed around the flowers and the grass. Sometimes, he tried to catch them with his hands, but they were too fast and smart. He felt frustrated when they escaped.

One day, he saw a big fly with shiny wings. It was different from the other flies. It looked like a tiny rainbow. Tommy wanted to see it better, so he followed it with his eyes. The fly flew from one plant to another, then to the fence, then to the tree. Tommy ran after it, but he could not reach it.

"Fly, fly, come here!" he shouted. "I want to be your friend!"

But the fly did not listen. It kept flying away from him. Tommy was sad and angry. He stomped his feet and cried.

"Tommy, what's wrong?" his mom asked. She came out of the house and saw him crying.

"Mommy, I want the fly!" he sobbed. "The pretty fly with the rainbow wings! But it won't let me catch it!"

His mom hugged him and wiped his tears. She looked at the fly and smiled.

"That's not a fly, Tommy. That's a butterfly. Butterflies are very shy and gentle. They don't like to be caught or touched. They like to be free and happy."

"Really?" Tommy asked. He looked at the butterfly again. It was still flying around the tree.

"Yes, really. But you can still watch them and admire them. They are very beautiful, aren't they?"

Tommy nodded. He felt a little better. He stopped crying and smiled.

"They are very beautiful, Mommy. Can we watch them together?"

"Of course, Tommy. Let's watch them together." His mom said. She took his hand and they sat on the grass. They watched the butterfly and the other flies in the garden. Tommy felt happy and curious. He learned a new word and a new thing. He liked butterflies.

"No, it is mine, I saw it first!" Lily said.

They pulled and tugged on the marble, but neither of them would let go. They started to yell and cry.

"Stop it, you two!" their mom said. "You are not being nice to each other. You need to support your friend, not fight with them. If you can't play with the marble together, I will take it away."

But Tom and Lily did not listen to their mom. They kept on fighting and pulling on the marble. They did not see the dog that was sleeping on the couch. The dog woke up and saw the marble. He thought it was a ball. He jumped off the couch and ran towards Tom and Lily.

The dog bit the marble and broke it in half. He chewed on the pieces and made them smaller and smaller. Tom and Lily stopped fighting and looked at the dog. They saw their special marble was gone. They felt very sad and sorry.

But it was too late. The marble was gone and they could not play with it anymore. They learned a hard lesson that day. They hugged each other and hoped to find another special marble someday.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the backyard. They liked to zoom them on the grass and pretend they were racing. Sometimes they made vroom-vroom noises and cheered for their cars.

One day, they saw a big puddle of water in the corner of the yard. It looked like a shiny oasis, where their cars could splash and cool off. Ben and Lily ran to the puddle with their cars and started to zoom them in the water.

"Look, my car is faster than yours!" Ben said to Lily.

"No, mine is faster!" Lily said back.

They zoomed their cars faster and faster, until they bumped into each other. The cars flew out of the puddle and landed on the dirt. They were wet and muddy and some of their wheels came off.

"Oh no, our cars are broken!" Ben and Lily cried.

They picked up their cars and tried to fix them, but they couldn't. They felt sad and angry. They blamed each other for ruining their cars.

"It's your fault, you zoomed too fast!" Ben said to Lily.

"No, it's your fault, you zoomed too close!" Lily said to Ben.

They started to argue and shout. They didn't want to play with each other anymore.

Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw their broken cars and their wet and muddy clothes. She saw their chubby faces and their frowny mouths.

"What happened here?" she asked.

Ben and Lily told her what happened. They both said it was the other's fault. They both said they didn't want to be friends anymore.

Mom shook her head and sighed. She said, "You two are silly. You were having so much fun with your cars, but you let a little bump ruin your day. You should have been more careful and more kind. You should have said sorry and helped each other. You should have remembered that your cars are just toys, but your friendship is more important."

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They felt ashamed and sorry. They realized that mom was right. They hugged each other and said sorry. They said they still wanted to be friends.

Mom smiled and said, "That's better. Now, let's go inside and clean up. Maybe we can find some glue and fix your cars. Or maybe we can find some new toys to play with. But remember, no matter what you play with, always play nice."

Ben and Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. We will."

They followed mom inside, holding hands and carrying their cars. They learned their lesson. They learned that zooming is fun, but friendship is more fun.

"Good job, Sara and Ben!" mom said. "Now we need to put the tray in the freezer for a little while, so the sandwiches don't get soggy. Can you help me carry the tray?"

Sara and Ben gasped and dropped the tray. The sandwiches fell on the floor and the paper flew everywhere. Mom looked shocked and confused.

"Pippa, how did you get in here?" mom asked. "And where did you come from?"

Pippa smiled and winked. "I came from the zoo, of course. I sneaked out when the keeper wasn't looking. I wanted to see the world and make some friends. And I found your freezer, which is nice and cold and full of yummy food. Do you mind if I stay for a while?"

"OK," Tom said. "But be careful. The well is deep and dark."

They ran to the well and looked inside. They could not see anything. Sara wanted to gain more water for her flowers. She pulled the rope and lowered the bucket.

"Can you hear the water?" she asked Tom.

"No," Tom said. "Maybe the well is empty."

Sara pulled the rope harder. She was careless and did not hold it tight. The rope slipped from her hand and the bucket fell into the well.

"Oh no!" Sara cried. "The bucket is gone!"

Tom tried to help her. He grabbed the rope and pulled it up. But the rope was too heavy and wet. He could not lift it.

"We need help," Tom said. "Let's go find a grown-up."

"Excuse me, sir," Sara said. "We need your help. We lost the bucket in the well."

"Yes, you can, bee. You are my friend. Here you go." Sara gave him a cup and a cookie. The bee drank and ate. He was happy.

"Yes, you can, ladybug. You are my friend. Here you go." Sara gave her a cup and a cookie. The ladybug drank and ate. She was happy.

Sara smiled and said, "I'm glad you came to my tea party. You are all very nice insects. Do you want to play with me?"

The ant, the bee and the ladybug nodded and said, "Yes, we do. You are a very kind girl. What do you want to play?"

Sara thought for a moment and said, "Let's play dress up. I have some hats and scarves and gloves in my house. Come, come, come!"

Sara laughed too and said, "You are the best insects ever. I love you. You make me happy."

"Put it down, Tom," Lily said. "That is not ours. We should not touch it."

"Stop it, Tom," Lily said. "You are breaking everything. We have to go."

The old man looked at Tom. He saw that he was honest too. He saw that he was scared too. He felt a little sorry for him too.

Lily and Tom thanked him. They ran out of the hut. They ran back to their home. They learned their lesson. They never went to the hut again. They never touched the axe again. They were good children. They were honest children.

"Hey, what are you doing with my radish?" It was Mr. Fox, who had seen her from his window. He was angry and ran towards her.

Lily was upset. She did not want to take off her new cloth. She liked it very much. She wanted to be a princess.

"But Mommy, I want to wear this cloth. It is pretty and I love it. Please, Mommy, please!" she begged.

Mommy was firm. She did not want Lily to catch a cold. She took the cloth from Lily and gave her the sweater and pants.

The bird nodded and looked worried. It pointed with its wing to the other side of the roof.

Mom and Dad said, "OK, then. Come on, let's go inside. We have to clean the wall. And you have to help us. And then you have to say sorry to the wall. And then you can have some oxygen and water. And then you can play with your crayons again. But only on paper. OK?"

Ben and Mia said, "OK, Mom. OK, Dad. We love you."

They hugged their parents and went inside. They felt sorry for the wall. They felt sorry for themselves. But they also felt glad. They knew their parents loved them. And they knew they would not mark on the wall again.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big hole in the ground near their house. They wondered what was inside. They decided to go and look.

They crawled into the hole and saw a dark tunnel. They heard a strange noise. They were scared, but curious. They wanted to find out what made the noise. They walked deeper into the tunnel.

They came to a big room with a lot of things. There were boxes, bags, cans, and bottles. There were also some toys, clothes, and books. They thought they had found a treasure. They started to take some things they liked.

Suddenly, they heard the noise again. It was louder and closer. They turned around and saw a big, hairy, angry man. He had a long beard, dirty clothes, and a stick. He was the one who lived in the hole. He was not happy to see the twins. He yelled at them and demanded that they give back his things. He waved his stick and chased them.

Tom and Lily were very scared. They dropped the things they had taken and ran for the exit. But they were too late. The man caught them and dragged them back to his room. He said they had to stay with him and be his slaves. He locked them in a cage and threw away the key. He said he would never let them go. He said they had to work for him and give him more things. He said he would hurt them if they tried to escape.

Tom and Lily cried and wished they had never gone into the hole. They missed their home, their parents, and their friends. They had no hope of being rescued. Lily and Ben were playing on the beach. They liked to dig in the sand and find shells. They had a bucket full of shells of different colors and shapes.

"Wow, Ben, that's a nice shell!" Lily said, admiring the shell. "Can I see it?"

Ben gave the shell to Lily. She looked at it closely and put her ear to the hole. She heard a soft sound, like the sea.

"Ben, I can hear the sea in the shell!" Lily said, smiling. "It's like magic!"

But then, something moved inside the shell. Lily felt a tickle in her ear and saw a claw poking out of the hole. She screamed and dropped the shell.

"Ouch, ouch, ouch!" a voice said from the shell. "Why did you disturb me? I was sleeping!"

Lily and Ben looked at the shell in surprise. A small crab crawled out of the hole and shook its claw at them. It had a dark shell that matched the big shell.

"Sorry, sorry, sorry!" Lily and Ben said, backing away. "We didn't know you were in the shell!"

The crab looked at them with angry eyes. "Well, now you know! This is my home, and I don't like visitors! Go away and leave me alone!"

The crab crawled back into the shell and hid in the hole. Lily and Ben ran away from the shell and decided to play with other shells that were empty and quiet. They learned not to disturb crabs that lived in shells.

Lily was not afraid. She liked to make new friends. She said, "Yes, you can stay with me. What is your name?"

"My name is Grace," the ghost said. "I like your name, Lily. It is a pretty flower."
