Tom and Mia were friends who liked to swim in the pool. One day, they saw a big basket of muffins on the table near the pool. They were hungry and wanted to eat some.

"Can we have some muffins, please?" Tom asked the lady who brought the basket.

"Sure, you can have one each, but only after you swim for a while. Muffins are a treat, not a meal," the lady said.

Tom and Mia nodded and jumped into the pool. They had fun splashing and playing with the toys. But soon, Tom got bored and wanted to eat a muffin.

"I don't want to swim anymore. I want a muffin now," Tom said to Mia.

"But the lady said we have to swim first. And swimming is good for us. It makes us strong and happy," Mia said.

"I don't care. I'm hungry and I like muffins. They are yummy and soft," Tom said. He climbed out of the pool and ran to the basket. He grabbed a muffin and took a big bite.

"Tom, stop! That's not fair! You have to share and follow the rules!" Mia shouted.

But Tom did not listen. He ate the whole muffin and reached for another one. He did not notice that the muffin he took was different from the others. It was green and had spots on it. It was a terrible muffin that was old and moldy.

Tom bit into the terrible muffin and made a face. He felt sick and spit out the muffin. He started to cry and hold his tummy.

"Mia, help me! This muffin is bad! It hurts!" Tom said.

Mia swam to the edge of the pool and saw Tom. She felt sorry for him, but also angry. She got out of the pool and went to the lady.

"Tom ate a terrible muffin and now he is sick. He did not swim and he did not share. He was greedy and naughty," Mia said.

The lady looked at Tom and saw the terrible muffin. She shook her head and sighed.

"Tom, you should have listened to me and Mia. You should have swum and waited for your treat. You should have been polite and fair. Now you have to learn your lesson. You have to drink some water and rest. And you have to say sorry to Mia and share the good muffins with her," the lady said.

Tom nodded and did what the lady said. He drank some water and lay down on a chair. He felt bad and ashamed. He said sorry to Mia and gave her a good muffin.

Mia smiled and accepted the muffin. She ate it and gave Tom a hug.

"It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. But next time, don't be greedy and naughty. Be kind and good. And always swim before you eat muffins," Mia said.

Tom hugged Mia back and agreed. He learned his lesson and never ate a terrible muffin again.

When he got closer, he heard some strange noises coming from inside. Tim peeked into the barrel and saw that there were animals inside! He saw rabbits and mice, all performing tricks and bouncing around. 

Tim was so amazed. He laughed and watched them perform. Suddenly the animals all stopped. They hopped out of the barrel and scurried away. 

Tim was still filled with joy and curiosity. He realized he had just witnessed the most magical thing he had ever seen in the dark forest. He would never forget what he saw in the mystery barrel!

The shopkeeper shook his head and smiled. He knew that the bunny had learnt his lesson: never take food without permission.

I will take your memory and put it in your car. It will not hurt. It will only take a moment." Tom did what the man said. He felt a tickle in his hand and a flash in his head. He opened his eyes and saw the man holding Zoom. Zoom looked new again. It had no crack and no missing wheel. It shone in the sun. It made a noise like beep.

Do not give it away easily. Only share it with those who deserve it. Those who love you and your car." He gave Zoom to Tom and smiled.

Tom was amazed and happy. He said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you. You are a good toy doctor. You are a good man. You are my friend too. Can I give you a hug?" The man said, "Of course you can. I like hugs. They are good for the heart." He hugged Tom and Zoom and said, "You are welcome, welcome, welcome. You are a good boy. You are a good friend. You have a good car. Take care of it and yourself. And have fun." He waved goodbye and walked away.

Tom waved goodbye and ran to the hill. He put Zoom on the top and pushed it hard. Zoom went very fast and flew in the air. Tom was happy and ran after Zoom. He made noises like vroom and beep. The bird looked at them and shook its head. It spoke in a strange voice.

"No, no, this is not your helicopter. This is my lunch. I like to eat ancient things. This helicopter is very ancient. It is made of metal and plastic. They are very tasty."

Tom and Amy were shocked. They didn't know what ancient meant, but they knew the bird was wrong. Their helicopter was not old, it was new. They got it for their birthday.

"That's not true!" Tom said. "Our helicopter is not ancient, it is new. We got it for our birthday. You can't eat it. It is not food, it is a toy. Give it back to us!"

The bird laughed and swallowed the helicopter. It burped and smiled.

"Too late, too late. I ate it. It was delicious. Thank you for your gift. Goodbye, children."

That night, a big storm came. The storm was very loud and scary. The rain came into Mia's room and filled the drawer. The expensive toy got all wet and broke. Mia was very sad and cried. She could not play with her favorite toy anymore.

In the tree, the bird saw a little girl. The girl said, "Hello, bird! Welcome to my tree. My name is Lily." The bird said, "Hello, Lily! My name is Sky."

Lily and Sky became friends. They liked to observe things together. They saw bugs, flowers, and other animals. They had a lot of fun in the big tree.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear who loved to jog. He would jog every day in the forest. He had many friends who would jog with him, like the rabbit, the squirrel, and the deer. They all liked to jog together.

One day, the sky turned dark and it started to rain. The big bear and his friends did not like to jog in the rain. So, they looked for a place to hide. They found a big tree with many leaves. The leaves helped to cover them from the rain. They all felt safe under the big tree.

As they waited for the rain to stop, they saw a slow snail. The snail was wet and cold. The big bear and his friends decided to help the snail. They used leaves to cover the snail and keep it warm. Soon, the rain stopped and they all went back to their slow and happy jog in the forest.

On their trip, Tim and his mom went to the park, the beach, and even the zoo. Tim brought his old blanket with him everywhere they went. At night, he would lay it out and they would sit on it, looking up at the stars.

One day, while they were at the beach, the wind blew Tim's old blanket away. Tim and his mom chased after it, laughing and playing. They finally caught up to the blanket and Tim hugged it tight. "I'm so glad we found my old blanket," he said.

At the end of their trip, Tim and his mom went back home. Tim unpacked his bag and put his old blanket on his bed. He knew that no matter where they went, his old blanket would always be with him.

Tim took the juice and poured it on the smelly sock. The juice made the sock wet, but it was not smelly anymore. Tim was happy. He had used his juice to make the sock smell better.

Tommy was playing outside in the garden. He saw a bird and he wanted to shoot it with his toy bow and arrow. He pulled back on the bow and released, but he missed. He was getting frustrated.

Suddenly, his mom came out and said, "Tommy, what are you doing?"

Tommy looked up and said, "I was trying to shoot the bird."

His mom shook her head and said, "No, Tommy, you can't shoot animals! That's not nice."

Tommy was feeling sad, but then his mom said, "I have a better idea. Why don't you shoot some balloons!" 

Tommy's eyes lit up, and he said excitedly, "Yes, mommy!"

His mom brought out some colorful balloons and set them up. Tommy pulled back his bow and shot the balloons one by one. He was having so much fun, and then he realized he had shot the last one.

Tommy was about to be frustrated, but then his mom said, "Look, Tommy, there's a surprise for you!" 

Tommy looked behind the last balloon and there was a baby doll. Tommy was so happy, he hugged and kissed the baby doll.

Tommy was no longer frustrated, he was happy and content.

The bear saw how hard Jack was trying to find a job and turn the tree into firewood. He appreciated Jack's hard work and gave him a real job to do. He said Jack could help him collect wood from the forest and offered him some of the wood from the tree.

Jack gladly accepted the job and thanked the bear for giving him a chance. The bear said that with hard work, Jack could make the job even better! 

Jack has been working with the bear ever since and he loves his job.

Once upon a time, there was a smart mouse who lived in the forest. He was very curious and loved to explore. 
One day, he decided to take an adventure and find out what lay beyond the trees. So he set off on a journey, determined to find something new.

As he wandered, he came across something odd. It was a big metal box, with a nail sticking out of the top. The clever mouse guessed that something must be inside the box, so he began to scratch away at the nail, trying to open it. 

It took him a long time, but eventually he managed to open the box and there, inside, was the most delicious cake he'd ever seen! It made his mouth water.

Resourcefully, the smart mouse realised he could use the nail to get inside the box and enjoy the cake.

From this experience, the mouse was able to take away an important lesson. He learned that being resourceful and smart can often lead to something amazing; it's always worth trying something new!

Once there was a little cricket who loved to run and play. He was so fast that everywhere he went, he made everyone smile.

One day, it was so hot outside that his friends were too tired to go and play. But the cricket still wanted to keep going, so he dashed out of the cool grass and onto the hot sand. 

Suddenly, he felt something that made him stop. It was a kind voice, telling him to turn back and head to the cool grass. The cricket listened and ran back, feeling strong and refreshed.

The cricket learned an important lesson that day. When it was hot, it was wise to stop and find a cool place to take a break. Taking care of himself, even during a fun time, kept him healthy and happy.

Once there was a small butterfly called Daisy. She was so foolish that she forgot to fly away when the sun was setting. So she lay on the grass in the park, waiting for morning.

Suddenly, she heard a tiny voice. She saw a 3 year old girl, who said: "Hello butterflies, I want to play!" Daisy was scared and tried to fly away, but the little girl was right behind her!

The girl said: "Please stay here butterfly. I want to be your friend!" Daisy lay still, feeling a bit foolish. She thought the best thing to do was to stay and listen to the little girl.

The girl said: "Let's play hide and seek! I will count to 10 and you can hide. I will never find you, silly butterfly!" Daisy flew off, looking for the perfect hiding spot. When she found it, she lay quietly behind a big bush. 

The little girl looked for Daisy for a really long time and finally gave up. She said: "Goodbye butterfly, maybe I'll see you tomorrow!" When the girl had gone, Daisy flew away. She thought to herself: "Next time I'll be more careful!"

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little bear named Steve. One day, Steve was walking through the woods when he heard the sound of someone talking. He was a very nosy bear and he wanted to know who was talking.

Steve slowly peered around the corner and saw a group of kids playing. One of them had lots of toys, and the other two were looking at him longingly. "I'm gonna spend all my money on this toy," the rich kid said. 

Steve's eyes lit up when he heard this. He was an eager bear and he wanted to spend some of that money. He slowly crept closer and closer, until he was standing right in front of them. 

"Hey!" he cried. "Can I get some of that money too?" 

The rich kid shook his head. "No way," he said. "It's mine, and I'm going to spend it all."

Steve was so angry that he began to shake and roar. The other kids quickly ran away, but Steve was too nosy. He stayed in the same spot, shaking and roaring until he collapsed. 

The day ended badly for nosy Steve. He had been so nosy that he'd run out of energy and collapsed in the middle of the woods.

Then a wise old owl flew close by and said, "Don't worry little baby, it's alright!"

The baby stopped crying and looked up at the owl. The owl said, "You must have dropped from the sky and I'm here to help. Where is your home?"

The baby smiled and said, "My home is far away, but I want to stay with you."

The wise old owl smiled and said, "Come on, I will take you home with me." So the wise old owl flew away with the baby in its talons, back to its nest. 

The baby thanked the owl for its help and settled down in the nest to make it its new home. From then on, the baby and the wise old owl were the best of friends.

Harry was a stubborn three-year-old. He didn't like to listen to his mum when he was told to do something, and he much rather play the whole day away.

One day, Harry's mum told him, "Harry, march to the park. I will meet you there with a surprise!"

But Harry wasn't interested. He didn't want to march anywhere - yet his mum insisted.

Harry shook his head and responded, "I don't wanna march, Mum!" 

"It's the truth," his Mum said firmly. "If you march, I will have a surprise waiting for you at the park. I promise!"

Harry was still hesitant, but eventually he marched, his steps slow and stubborn.

Finally, after a good long march, Harry arrived at the park. And sure enough, just like his mum had said, there was a surprise waiting for him - an ice-cream!

There was one lesson Harry learned that day: truth can be trusted. He now knows that if his Mum says something, it will be true - no matter how stubborn he is when asked to do something.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Faith was walking through the woods. She wanted to explore and see the things that the wild animals made. As Faith walked, she saw a big log lying on the ground. She wanted to try and lift it, so she pushed and pulled with all her strength. But try as she might, Faith could not lift the log.

Suddenly, a small fox stepped out from the trees. The fox was very obedient and it helped Faith lift the log. With both of them working together, they were able to move the log. Faith was so happy.

She thanked the fox and asked it to come along with her. But the fox shook its little head and scampered off into the woods. Faith was sad she couldn't keep her new friend, but she was also glad that she was able to lift the log. 

The two were never seen again, but Faith always remembered the little fox who had been so obedient and helpful.
